title: Only you know what is in your heart
odia: ମାଲୁଣି ହାତରେ ଲଙ୍କା ମରିଚଲୋ, ମାଳି ହାତେ ଫୁଲ ହାର, ଯାହା ମନ କଥା, ସିଏ ଜାଣେ ସିନା, ତାହା କି ଜାଣିବ ପର ॥
literal_meaning: Chillies in the woman gardener’s hand, a flower garland in the gardener’s hand: each person knows their own thoughts; how would another know them?
explanation: The closing lines remind us that another person’s private thoughts are not directly visible. The everyday objects lead into that contrast; this reading does not assign a hidden moral meaning to the chillies or garland. Ask rather than assume what someone feels.
meaning_odia: ହାତରେ ଥିବା ଲଙ୍କା ବା ଫୁଲହାର ଦିଶୁଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ମନର କଥା ସେମିତି ଦିଶେନାହିଁ। ଜଣେ କଣ ଭାବୁଛନ୍ତି ବା ଅନୁଭବ କରୁଛନ୍ତି, ତାହା ସେ ନିଜେ ଭଲ ଜାଣନ୍ତି। ତେଣୁ ବାହାରର ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ଦେଖି ମନ କଥା ଧରିନେବା ଅପେକ୍ଷା ପଚାରି ଶୁଣିବା ଭଲ। ଏହି ପାଠରେ ଲଙ୍କା ଓ ଫୁଲକୁ ଅଲଗା ନୈତିକ ଅର୍ଥ ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ।
usage_example: A friend seems quiet after receiving good news. Rather than decide that they are ungrateful, you ask what is on their mind. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: Listed as a saying in this community anthology; author, earliest use and possible song or literary relationships remain unverified. Gardener words are translated as occupational imagery, not evidence about any community’s traits.
